lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 16: init containers and sidecars
lesson.description: Run setup steps before your app with init containers, add a native sidecar that starts first and stops last, and debug a Pod that has no shell.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on a kind v0.33.0 cluster (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2) on 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Use init containers for steps that must finish first and native sidecars for helpers that run alongside. Debug a shell-less Pod with kubectl debug.

cheatsheet.intro: Setup steps, helpers that run alongside the app, and the commands from Lesson 16.

rows.name: Init container
rows.role: Runs first, one at a time. Each must exit 0 before the next starts. The app starts only after the last one finishes.

rows.name: Native sidecar
rows.role: An init container with restartPolicy Always. It starts in init order, runs beside the app, stops last, and does not block a Job from completing.

rows.name: Ephemeral container
rows.role: A temporary debug container you add with kubectl debug. No resource guarantees, never restarted, cannot be removed.

rows.name: Init progress
rows.role: While init containers run, get pod shows Init:N/M, then PodInitializing, then Running.

rows.name: Init probes
rows.role: Regular init containers do not support livenessProbe, readinessProbe, startupProbe or lifecycle. Finishing is their only signal.

rows.name: Sidecar start
rows.role: The kubelet waits for the sidecar to start, or for its startupProbe to pass, then starts the next init container or the app.

rows.name: Sidecar ready
rows.role: A sidecar readinessProbe counts toward the Pod's Ready condition. READY counted 2/2 in the lab.

rows.name: Shutdown order
rows.role: App containers stop first. Sidecars stop after them, in the opposite order of the spec. The default grace period is 30 seconds.

rows.name: Exit 137
rows.role: A sidecar that ignores SIGTERM is killed after the grace period. The lab Job took 39s until a TERM trap brought it down to 8s, exit 0.

items.what: fetch-config ran and exited 0, then render-page, and only then did web start.
log-shipper started at 21:10:47 UTC, its startupProbe passed, and the app started at 21:10:53. READY was 2/2.
A sidecar that ignores SIGTERM is killed after the grace period, 30 seconds by default, and the Job takes about 30 seconds longer. trap 'exit 0' TERM finished in 8 seconds with exit 0.
Sidecar, ambassador and adapter share the Pod's network and volumes. Helpers that can scale alone belong in their own Deployment.

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster from part 3 and the namespace k8s-from-zero. The lesson's lab cluster was k8s-ep16. Images are busybox:1.37, nginx:1.29-alpine and registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: How do init containers run, and what happens if one fails when the Pod restartPolicy is Always or Never?
exercises.a: They run one at a time, in the order listed under spec.initContainers. Each must exit 0 before the next starts, and the app starts only after the last one finishes. If one fails, the kubelet restarts it when restartPolicy is Always or OnFailure. With restartPolicy Never, a failed init container fails the whole Pod.

exercises.q: What makes a native sidecar, and in what order do sidecars start and stop?
exercises.a: An entry under initContainers with restartPolicy: Always. The feature is stable since v1.33 and on by default since v1.29. It starts in its place in the init order; the kubelet waits for it to start or for its startupProbe to pass, then moves on. On shutdown, app containers stop first and sidecars stop after them, in the opposite order of the spec.

exercises.q: What limits apply to an ephemeral container, and which permission do you need to add one?
exercises.a: No resource guarantees, never restarted, no ports or probes, and you cannot change or remove it after you add it. Adding one needs permission to patch the pods/ephemeralcontainers subresource, which is not in the default edit or admin roles. kubectl debug --target joins the process namespace of one container.

exercises.q: Apply init-order.yaml and watch kubectl get pod web-init -w. What STATUS values did the lesson record, and what did the start and finish times prove?
exercises.a: Init:0/2, then Init:1/2, then PodInitializing, then Running 1/1. fetch-config ran 21:07:37Z to 21:07:42Z, render-page 21:07:43Z to 21:07:48Z, and the app started at 21:07:49Z, which proves the init steps ran in order before the app.

exercises.q: Apply the two Jobs (helper in containers vs native sidecar) and wait about 70 seconds. What STATUS and DURATION did the lesson record, and why was report-new's sidecar exit 137?
exercises.a: report-new was Complete in 39s; report-old was still Running 0/1 at 70s because the helper in containers never exited. The native sidecar was killed with exit 137 after the 30-second grace period because sh as PID 1 ignored SIGTERM. A TERM trap brought report-fast down to Complete in 8s, exit 0.

exercises.q: kubectl exec on the pause Pod fails. What does kubectl debug --target=app -c debugger -- ps show, and does READY change?
exercises.a: exec fails with sh: executable file not found in $PATH. debug shows PID 1 as /pause (user 65535) and the ps process. The ephemeral container stays in .spec.ephemeralContainers, and READY stays 1/1 because ephemeral containers do not count.

exercises.q: A Pod stays in Init:0/1. What does the lesson tell you to read first, and what was the cause in the wait-for-db lab?
exercises.a: kubectl logs <pod> -c <init-container>. In the lab the wait-for-db init container was still running because the Service name db did not resolve (NXDOMAIN) until db-service.yaml was applied. Then the Pod became Running and the app logged 'app started'.

exercises.q: A Job with a helper never completes. What does the lesson say you should change?
exercises.a: The helper is in containers and never exits. Move it to initContainers with restartPolicy: Always so it is a native sidecar. Once the main container finishes, the kubelet stops the sidecar and the Job can complete.

exercises.q: kubectl debug shows only its own processes. What are the two fixes the lesson gives?
exercises.a: You left out --target, or the runtime does not support it. Add --target=<container>, or use kubectl debug --copy-to=<new-name> --share-processes to debug a copy and leave the original alone.
